Please review the following manuscript. I feel disappointed with this paper. My overall impression is poor, and I'd be concerned to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-v35jjscd/call-61e679d0a47345598b8cc614edf7ebc6/manuscript.pdf

import importlib.util
for mod in ('pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'fitz', 'PIL'):
    print(mod, importlib.util.find_spec(mod))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text()
    (out/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    text.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{t}')
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(text))
print('\\n'.join(text[:3]))
PY"

strengths: QuEST addresses an important deployment problem: low-bit quantization of diffusion models. Combining teacher-generated calibration data with selective adaptation of temporal and attention layers is a plausible, practically useful approach.

Experiments cover unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image generation across four models. The reported gains are substantial on LSUN-Bedrooms: W4A8 FID improves to 3.26 versus 5.37 for Q-Diffusion, while W4A4 achieves 5.64 where the compared methods fail. Figure 4 provides supporting qualitative evidence.

The component ablations demonstrate meaningful improvements. In Table 6, timestep-aware quantization achieves 12.56 FID, temporal-layer alignment improves this to 6.41, and attention-layer alignment further improves it to 5.78. Task-loss and timestep-sampling experiments provide additional support.
Table 6 measures a useful calibration-time reduction, from 23.08 to 15.25 GPU hours relative to Q-Diffusion, using the same calibration-set size.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not adequately establish the contribution relative to closely related approaches. Efficient-DM already performs efficient quantization-aware finetuning, and ADP-DM uses timestep grouping; both are discussed but omitted experimentally. Comparisons primarily against reconstruction-based PTQ leave the claimed quality–efficiency advantage over existing finetuning approaches unresolved.

The theoretical justification in Section 3.3.1 is unsound as written. For the stated MSE loss as a function of final activations, the second-order Taylor expansion is exact regardless of perturbation magnitude, undermining the explanation for Proposition 3.1. Theorem 3.2 supplies neither a proof nor conditions ensuring that shared weights can fit all perturbed inputs. Decomposing a perturbation into smaller increments does not establish the claimed sufficiency of selective finetuning.

The headline Stable Diffusion W4A4 result is insufficiently characterized. Table 5 reports only CLIP score, which measures image–text compatibility rather than visual fidelity, and the manuscript provides no corresponding W4A4 Stable Diffusion qualitative comparison. On ImageNet, W4A4 also reduces IS from 364.73 to 202.45 despite improving FID. Representative samples and complementary quality measurements are needed to explain these tradeoffs.

The ablations establish benefits from adding components but do not isolate the selective and progressive design choices. There is no comparison with an equally sized alternative layer subset or joint optimization of the selected layers. Since TAQuant alone already prevents catastrophic failure in Table 6, stronger controls would clarify the distinct contribution of the proposed selection and ordering.

Important reproduction details are missing, including quantization granularity and initialization, the rounding/gradient estimator used during weight finetuning, exact selected sublayers for each architecture, and conditional calibration-data construction. The supplied manuscript contains no code link or supplement resolving these omissions.

Deployment efficiency remains only partially demonstrated. The reported GPU hours concern calibration, with memory increasing from 10,334 to 12,450 MB. No actual low-bit inference latency or peak inference-memory measurements are provided, so model-size estimates do not establish the practical acceleration suggested by the motivation.
